title: Morning Edition
notes: Morning Edition for Tuesday, Nov 3, 2026 — U.S. midterm Election Day. It leads with polls opening across the country. Results are not in yet; we describe voting as under way and keep scheduled language for closings.

The U.S. has three stories (Election Day, the Justice Department’s 50-state monitoring plan, and flood-driven polling-place moves). Canada, Hong Kong, China and World have three each. Stories already in Monday’s Evening Edition were not repeated.

Culture and sports appear outside the U.S. this morning (a Mulroney documentary prize, the Wuzhen internet summit, and Formula 1’s youngest champion). The U.S. section is election-heavy; we did not pad it with thin entertainment items.
Some pages blocked automated fetches (noted under Sources & checks); that is an access limit, not a broken link.
provenance: U.S. Election Day figures for early votes differ slightly by outlet and update time (CBS/University of Florida Voting Lab: more than 57 million; BBC citing the same lab later Monday night: about 58.7 million). We use the more than 57 million figure and note the range.
China stock-support claims lean on Xinhua (state media) plus Caixin; PBOC rate-shift detail is from Caixin, with limited article body behind a paywall/snippet.

stories.headline: Polls open across the U.S. as voters decide control of Congress on midterm Election Day
stories.deck: Election Day voting is under way after more than 57 million Americans cast early ballots. All 435 House seats and 35 Senate seats are on the ballot; Democrats need to flip a handful of seats in each chamber to take control from Republicans.
stories.summary: Election Day voting is under way after more than 57 million Americans cast early ballots, according to the University of Florida Voting Lab as reported by CBS News. All 435 House seats and 35 Senate seats are on the ballot, and 36 states are electing governors. Democrats need to flip three House seats and four Senate seats to wrest control from Republicans, per AP and CBS. The first polling stations opened in Vermont at 5 a.m. ET, BBC reported, with East Coast states including New York, New Jersey, Virginia and Maine opening at 6 a.m. NPR said more than 54 million people had already voted by early Tuesday and that Democrats are favored to win the House while the Senate remains anyone’s guess. Results are scheduled to start arriving after polls close this evening; many close races may take days to call. The Supreme Court on Monday denied the Trump administration’s emergency request to make California set aside about 20,000 disputed mail ballots — covered in Monday’s Evening Edition.
stories.why: Control of Congress will shape how much of President Trump’s agenda can advance in the final two years of his term — and whether Democrats can block or investigate it.
stories.label: Reported
stories.note: No results are in as of this morning edition. Early-vote totals move through the day; BBC cited about 58.7 million as of late Monday night from the same Florida lab CBS used for the 57 million-plus figure.

stories.headline: Justice Department deploys about 1,000 election monitors to all 50 states for the first time
stories.deck: In a Tuesday morning release, the Justice Department said it is mounting its largest Election Day monitoring effort ever — about 1,000 monitors and observers, for the first time covering every state — to check compliance with federal voting-rights laws.
stories.summary: In a Tuesday morning release, the Justice Department said it is mounting its largest Election Day monitoring effort ever — about 1,000 monitors and observers, for the first time covering every state. The Civil Rights Division is coordinating the deployment, which includes Division staff, other DOJ components, U.S. Attorney’s Offices and federal observers from the Office of Personnel Management. Assistant Attorney General Harmeet K. Dhillon said the department is “deploying the largest monitoring effort in DOJ history” and pursuing “transparency for elections in an assertive and nondiscriminatory manner.” Monitors are to check compliance with statutes including the Voting Rights Act, National Voter Registration Act, Help America Vote Act, Uniformed and Overseas Citizens Absentee Voting Act, Civil Rights Acts and the ADA; the release lists jurisdictions in all 50 states. CBS News also reported the 50-state plan early Tuesday.
stories.why: A first-time nationwide DOJ presence on Election Day is a major administrative move on a day when trust in election administration is itself a campaign issue.
stories.label: Official statement + reported
stories.note: The release describes observation and complaint channels; it does not say monitors will run elections or change local procedures.

stories.headline: Flooding and storms force polling-place moves in Florida and elsewhere on Election Day
stories.deck: At least 18 polling locations in seven Florida counties were relocated after flash flooding, NBC News reported. A tornado damaged an Oklahoma polling site, and flood-hit counties in Utah and Colorado were given special ballot options.
stories.summary: At least 18 polling locations across seven Florida counties — Brevard, Highlands, Indian River, Martin, Okeechobee, Palm Beach and St. Lucie — were moved after intense rainfall caused flash floods Monday into Tuesday morning, NBC News reported. Some coastal areas saw as much as 22 inches of rain in 24 hours; Gov. Ron DeSantis declared a state of emergency in the seven counties. BBC, citing its partner CBS, separately said Florida election officials were temporarily relocating 19 polling stations under that order. In Oklahoma, Cimarron County moved a polling place after a Sunday tornado damaged the Keyes Community Center. Utah’s lieutenant governor and Colorado’s secretary of state authorized special electronic-ballot options for flood-isolated voters in San Juan County, Utah, and La Plata and Archuleta counties, Colorado. Weather’s effect on turnout is being watched, though researchers note early and mail voting have softened rain’s historical impact.
stories.why: Even limited polling-place moves can confuse voters in competitive states — and become fodder for election-integrity arguments online.
stories.label: Reported + official statement
stories.note: BBC’s “19” and NBC’s “at least 18” are close but not identical counts of Florida moves; both attribute the authority to DeSantis’s emergency order.

stories.headline: After a big re-election win, Olivia Chow seeks a new long-term funding deal with Ontario
stories.deck: Toronto’s mayor, re-elected with more than 500,000 votes, is preparing to press Premier Doug Ford for a successor to the 2023 “new deal” as chunks of provincial support expire and the city faces a budget shortfall that could reach about $1.1 billion.
stories.summary: Toronto’s mayor, re-elected with more than 500,000 votes, is preparing to press Premier Doug Ford for a successor to the 2023 “new deal” as chunks of provincial support expire and the city faces a budget shortfall that could reach about $1.1 billion, CBC News reported. That earlier agreement included billions in relief over three years and Ontario’s takeover of the Gardiner Expressway and Don Valley Parkway. Councillor Shelley Carroll said city hall wants “long-term measures” rather than a one-off cheque. Ford said after the municipal election that Ontario had given Toronto “more money than any government in the history of Ontario,” but Municipal Affairs Minister Rob Flack said Monday he was not aware of specific talks and that a decision on entering a second deal “hasn’t been fully made yet,” waiting until Chow is sworn in again in mid-November. Ontario last week raised its 2026-27 deficit forecast to $16.9 billion and pushed balance to 2029-30.
stories.why: Canada’s largest city is trying to lock in stable provincial support just as Queen’s Park’s own books are worsening.
stories.label: Reported

stories.headline: B.C. First Nations go to court over Pacific Link’s ‘national interest’ designation
stories.deck: Several First Nations, including the St’át’imc Chiefs Council, filed federal judicial reviews seeking to overturn Ottawa’s decision to list the Alberta-to-B.C. oil pipeline as a project of national interest under the Building Canada Act.
stories.summary: Several First Nations, including the St’át’imc Chiefs Council representing 11 communities, filed federal judicial reviews seeking to overturn Ottawa’s decision to list the Pacific Link oil pipeline as a project of national interest under the Building Canada Act, CBC News reported Monday. The proposed line would move about one million barrels a day from Bruderheim, Alta., to a deepwater port near Delta, B.C. Listing shifts the federal focus from whether to build to how, by fast-tracking approvals. The nations argue the listing “effectively acts as an approval” and that duty-to-consult obligations must be met before a project is listed. Chief Bonnie Adolph said her community was refused consultation because its territory is not directly on the route, despite Fraser River watershed concerns. Other applicants include Boston Bar, Cheam, Lower Nicola, Kwantlen, Kwikwetlem, Skeetchestn and Tsartlip, plus Cold Lake First Nations in Alberta. Pacific Link said Indigenous participation, including possible equity ownership, is central to the project. CBC said it had sought a federal response.
stories.why: A court fight over consultation could slow one of the Carney government’s marquee energy projects.
stories.label: Reported + allegation
stories.note: The nations’ claim that Canada breached its duty to consult is their court argument, not a finding.

stories.headline: Satirical Brian Mulroney documentary wins Windsor film festival’s top Canadian prize
stories.deck: Matthew Rankin’s Ladies and Gentlemen, Brian Mulroney took the $25,000 WIFF Prize in Canadian Film. The archival collage film, a TIFF Midnight Madness audience favourite, looks at how Mulroney’s public image was built.
stories.summary: Matthew Rankin’s Ladies and Gentlemen, Brian Mulroney took the $25,000 WIFF Prize in Canadian Film at the Windsor International Film Festival, The Canadian Press reported via CBC. The documentary, which premiered at TIFF and was an audience favourite in Midnight Madness, splices archival footage of Mulroney before he reached 24 Sussex with multimedia collage. The jury praised its “uniquely Canadian voice, and intelligence and humour,” and singled out archive producer Marika Lapointe, who sifted more than 80,000 pieces of material. Rankin has said the film is “not exactly a biopic” but “about the construction of his image.” Mulroney, Canada’s Progressive Conservative prime minister in the 1980s and early 1990s, died in 2024 at 84.
stories.why: A major Canadian festival prize keeps a stylized political documentary in the awards conversation heading into awards season.
stories.label: Reported

stories.headline: Beijing formally removes Winnie Ho as Hong Kong housing secretary after Tai Po fire resignation
stories.deck: China’s State Council approved Chief Executive John Lee’s recommendation to remove Ho Wing-yin, who resigned Oct 28 saying she would take political responsibility for the Wang Fuk Court fire. No successor was named in the announcements.
stories.summary: China’s State Council approved Chief Executive John Lee’s recommendation to remove Ho Wing-yin as Secretary for Housing, Xinhua and the Hong Kong government said Tuesday. Ho resigned on Oct 28, saying she would “shoulder the political accountability” for the Wang Fuk Court fire in Tai Po. Lee’s statement praised her work since 2022, including Light Public Housing, shortening the composite waiting time for subsidised rental housing from 6.1 to 4.8 years, and the Basic Housing Units Ordinance. RTHK noted the removal followed last week’s independent committee report and reform package. The State Council announcement gave no reason beyond the Basic Law process and did not name a successor.
stories.why: Formal removal closes the political-accountability chapter for the housing chief after one of Hong Kong’s deadliest residential fires.
stories.label: Official statement + state media

stories.headline: Hong Kong launches one-stop check-in for Hangzhou and Wuhan flights via the airport
stories.deck: Transport Secretary Mable Chan said a pilot lets travellers from those mainland airports check bags through to overseas destinations via Hong Kong without reclaiming luggage, as part of a national “trunk-branch” aviation programme.
stories.summary: Transport Secretary Mable Chan said a pilot lets travellers from Hangzhou Xiaoshan and Wuhan Tianhe check in for their whole journey and transfer through Hong Kong International Airport without reclaiming luggage, even on a different airline for the onward leg, RTHK reported. Speaking at the Super Terminal Expo opening, Chan called the scheme “game-changing” and said the mainland transfer platform already covers more than 260 airports and has handled over 260 million transfer passengers. She framed it as embedding Hong Kong in the national aviation architecture and restated a five-year aim to grow Hong Kong’s network from about 220 to 240 destinations. SCMP also reported the Tuesday launch for Hangzhou and Wuhan passengers.
stories.why: Easier mainland-to-world connections via Hong Kong are meant to reinforce the city’s hub role — and feed airline and airport traffic.

stories.headline: Hong Kong pledges one-stop liaison officers for homeowners on building renovations
stories.deck: Acting housing chief Michael Wong told lawmakers liaison officers would handle enquiries and complaints on major maintenance works, part of reforms after the Wang Fuk Court fire, with AI proposed only to flag document anomalies for human review.
stories.summary: Acting housing chief Michael Wong told a Legislative Council housing panel that liaison officers would be assigned as a single contact for owners’ corporations and homeowners on major renovation projects, RTHK reported. The pledge follows last week’s reform package after the Wang Fuk Court fire that killed 168 people. Project-specific teams are planned, and the Housing Bureau’s Independent Checking Unit is to be replaced by a Public Housing Building Control Section this month. Wong said AI could audit large document sets in fractions of a second to flag anomalies, but “will not make the final judgement.”
stories.why: Clearer homeowner contacts are a practical test of whether post-fire building-safety reforms change daily experience at estates under repair.

stories.headline: China readies a third market-support swap and makes buyback lending permanent
stories.deck: The PBOC said it would run another Securities, Funds and Insurance companies Swap Facility operation on Tuesday, with applications topping 100 billion yuan. Share-buyback relending becomes a long-term tool and its rate falls to 1%.
stories.summary: The PBOC said it would run a third Securities, Funds and Insurance companies Swap Facility (SFISF) operation on Tuesday, with a one-year term that can be extended; 31 securities and fund firms applied for more than 100 billion yuan (about $14.9 billion), Xinhua reported. After a meeting with the financial regulator and CSRC, the central bank said it would expand participants, lower swap fees and refine collateral rules. The share-buyback and stake-increase relending facility, launched as a temporary 2024 tool, becomes a long-term arrangement and its relending rate drops from 1.25% to 1%. Xinhua said signed buyback-related loans total about 440 billion yuan, with more than 280 billion disbursed. Caixin also reported the package as support for a declining stock market.
stories.why: Beijing is leaning on liquidity tools again as it tries to stabilise equities without a dramatic policy U-turn.
stories.label: State media + reported

stories.headline: PBOC makes the overnight reverse-repo rate its main policy rate at 1.25%
stories.deck: China’s central bank shifted its primary policy rate from the seven-day to the overnight reverse-repo rate effective Monday, conducting daily fixed-rate overnight operations, Caixin reported.
stories.summary: China’s central bank shifted its primary policy rate from the seven-day to the overnight reverse-repo rate effective Monday, Caixin reported. The PBOC now runs overnight reverse-repo operations every working day at a fixed rate through quantity bidding; the rate stands at 1.25%. Seven-day operations are to be used mainly around tax deadlines and month-ends. Governor Pan Gongsheng had previewed the change in September, saying the overnight rate DR001 had effectively become the target.
stories.why: A clearer overnight policy rate is meant to tighten the link between central-bank settings and money-market pricing.

stories.headline: Oil falls more than 7% as U.S. and Iran signal openness to talks
stories.deck: Brent settled near $104.77 and WTI near $96.46 after Tehran and Washington pointed to diplomacy over the eight-month war that has largely closed the Strait of Hormuz shipping lane.
stories.summary: Brent crude fell about 7.6% to settle at $104.77 a barrel and U.S. WTI about 7.4% to $96.46, CNBC reported, after U.S. and Iranian officials signalled openness to a negotiated end to their eight-month war. President Trump said Iran wants to “make a deal and that could happen”; Iran’s President Masoud Pezeshkian said Tehran is seeking dialogue, and Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said intensive mediated consultations continue, per state media cited by CNBC and the Guardian. The Guardian earlier Monday had Brent as low as about $105.55 intraday. Vice President JD Vance spoke of “good conversations” and a possible “negotiated settlement,” while Trump had warned of “the hammer” if progress fails. Analysts cautioned that without a concrete ceasefire, risk premium may only partly fade.
stories.why: Cheaper crude would ease a global inflation shock — but past Iran-war false dawns have quickly reversed.
stories.label: Reported + claim
stories.note: Peace-talk progress is asserted by officials on both sides; no agreement has been announced.

stories.headline: Cyberattacks hit supermarket fridges across nine European countries
stories.deck: Remote tampering switched refrigeration into defrost mode, spoiling food from Belgium to Sweden. Belgian federal prosecutors opened a criminal investigation; the EU agriculture commissioner called it a deliberate threat to the food supply chain.
stories.summary: Suspected cyberattacks on Nov 2 hit grocery refrigeration systems in at least nine countries — Belgium, Estonia, Finland, Ireland, Italy, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Portugal and Sweden — Euronews reported, forcing some stores to discard food after temperatures rose overnight. Belgium was among the hardest hit, with dozens of Delhaize, Carrefour, Intermarché and Spar outlets affected; federal prosecutors opened a criminal probe, VRT confirmed. Attackers reportedly switched evaporators to defrost mode, a pattern refrigeration firms linked to an October attack on French chains. Danish supplier Danfoss said outdated software left some customers exposed. EU Agriculture Commissioner Christophe Hansen said the incidents were “a deliberate attempt to disrupt our food supply chain.” No one has claimed responsibility.
stories.why: A cross-border hit on cold chains shows how everyday connected equipment can become critical infrastructure overnight.
stories.label: Reported + official statement

stories.headline: Kimi Antonelli becomes Formula 1’s youngest world champion at the Mexico City GP
stories.deck: The 20-year-old Mercedes driver sealed the title with third place behind Max Verstappen and Lewis Hamilton, breaking Sebastian Vettel’s age record and becoming Italy’s first champion since 1953.
stories.summary: Kimi Antonelli sealed his first Formula 1 world title at 20 years and 68 days by finishing third at the Mexico City Grand Prix, BBC Sport and Reuters/Al Jazeera reported. Red Bull’s Max Verstappen won a red-flagged race and Ferrari’s Lewis Hamilton was second after a tense first-lap fight with teammate Charles Leclerc. Antonelli’s championship lead became unassailable at 119 points; he broke Sebastian Vettel’s record as youngest champion by more than three years and is the first Italian title winner since Alberto Ascari in 1953. The race included two safety cars and a long stoppage after Valtteri Bottas crashed. Mercedes leads the constructors’ standings heading to Brazil.
stories.why: A teenage-to-twenties title rewrite marks a changing of the guard in F1’s driver hierarchy.
stories.label: Reported
